threads: the library's default (the device's fast cores, at most 4); the CLI check runs --threads 4
calls: calls.json: <run> → {calls: [{index, start, end, rc, error, buffer_start, dropped, out}], stop: {rc, error, out}}; start and end delimit the samples fed (from the stream start), rc is the return code
audio: lead_samples zeros, then the clips (testdata/audio, int16 / 32768) with gap_samples zeros between consecutive clips; pcm_sha256 is the SHA-256 of those float32 samples, little-endian. The calls cut them into chunk_samples (the last call shorter) or into call_samples. Every run is one stream that ends with a stop, so the next run starts a new one
output: out is the engine's JSON with pass_ms dropped (a timing), keys sorted, values verbatim. text is the committed text of all calls and the stop joined by spaces, stop_language the stop's language
checks: outside the edge set the run fails unless every call returns rc ≥ 0, rc equals the number of words, text is the words joined by spaces, received is the samples fed so far / 16000 rounded to two decimals either way, and pass_ms is > 0 on every process call and 0.0 on every stop
buffer_start: buffer_start (samples from the stream start), on calls that committed words: the start t0 of the audio [t0, end) whose needle_transcribe JSON (in the run's language) ends with this call's words (the same text, start and end once shifted by t0, and probability) followed by the words of pending, in the same language. Candidates in order: the previous call's t0 (0 at first), then the ends of earlier committed words after it, newest first, as long as [t0, end) is at most 30 s. dropped is the number of words of that JSON before the call's words, which the engine left out as already committed. Both absent when the call committed nothing or no candidate matched
cli_check: "same": needle --audio-stream --audio-chunk <chunk_samples / 16000> [--audio-language] --audio-word-timestamps --threads 4 on the run's samples as a float WAV prints, after dropping pass_ms, exactly the outputs of the calls with rc > 0 followed by the stop's; the run fails otherwise. Not run on the edge set
offline: offline is testdata/oracle/<clip>.json's text, for the long runs the clips' texts joined by spaces; offline_word_errors is the word-level edit distance from it to text (words split at spaces)
